title: Barth's simple summary
hookLine: Karl Barth, asked to sum up his vast theology, is remembered for naming a children's song, Jesus loves me

lines: SUM IT UP IN ONE SENTENCE.
cards: Karl Barth wrote theology by the shelf. His great work, the Church Dogmatics, fills thick volume after thick volume, and he never finished it.
The story goes that on a lecture visit, a student asked him to sum up his whole life's work in a single sentence.
And Barth, the story says, answered with a song from childhood: "Jesus loves me! this I know, for the Bible tells me so."
The story is told in more than one version, and people still argue about exactly where and when he said it. But it stuck, maybe because of the surprise in it.

teach.b: It sounds like a dodge. It isn't. Barth's theology turns on one conviction: we don't climb up to God; God comes down to us.

Everything starts with God speaking, God acting, God loving first, in Jesus Christ. That's why he argued so hard with theologians who began from human experience, Schleiermacher among them, whom this path met last week.
Now take the song word by word. Jesus: the center is a person, not an idea. Loves: the first thing God says to us is yes.
Me: a person, not humanity in general. This I know, for the Bible tells me so: the knowing isn't something worked out alone; it was told, handed over, given.

The first letter of John puts it the same way round: "We love him, because he first loved us." And, shorter still: "God is love." Barth's critics found him hard going, and sometimes too sure of himself.
His admirers say the thick volumes are, in a way, one long commentary on that children's line. Christians read him both ways.

teach.h: THE HEART, IN A CHILD'S SONG
teach.b: Either way, the scene stays: a man who could talk for volumes, asked for the heart of it all, reached for words a child could sing.

how: "Jesus Loves Me" is sung in Sunday schools and children's services across different churches, and some adults sing or say it as a short prayer of trust.

games.q: you've written theology by the shelf. a student asks you to sum up your whole life's work in one sentence. what do you say?
o: Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so.
games.why: that's the answer the story gives Barth: a song from childhood, the whole thing in words a child can sing.

practice: If you know the old children's song, sing its first line quietly and slowly, or just say it or hear it in your head: Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so.
If you're here to learn rather than to pray, notice what each word claims, without needing to agree. Let each word land before the next, then rest in the quiet after.

carryVoice: Your line: Jesus loves me. A whole theology, small enough for a child to sing. See you tomorrow.
